scope: Bounded static audit of direct E530 callers in official CnCNetYR-Hardened v0.0.0.17. No target execution/modification, no bypass implementation, no exception-handler recovery test.

prior_condition_semantics.use: Names for previously established integrity conditions; this audit does not expand their original-game reverse engineering.

direct_call_search.method: Scan E8/E9 rel32 candidates, then verify all four in bounded instruction disassembly.
direct_call_search.limitation: Does not establish absence of computed/indirect transfers or later dynamic rewriting.

semantics: S = global[RVA37DB4] OR incomingEDX OR incomingECX OR global[RVA37DB8].
ESP=S; EDI=0; temporary T=oldEBP OR S; ECX=(oldECX+T) modulo2^32; EAX=oldEAX OR T; EBP=0.
JMP EBP transfers control to zero; no return instruction exists in this body.
fatal_routine.distinction: The helper body deliberately does not return normally. That does not prove its callers were compiled with a noreturn declaration: all four observed CALLs retain meaningful fallthrough and caller cleanup.
fatal_routine.abi: The body deliberately violates ordinary returning-function preservation of ESP/EBP/EDI. ECX and EAX are also modified. Restoring only an instruction pointer cannot reconstruct the caller state.
fatal_routine.exception_delivery_limit: A manufactured ESP is not a valid-stack guarantee. These constants are potential signature evidence if captured in a crash context; no guarantee Windows will deliver a usable handler, dialog, stack walk, or recoverable context.

callers.fallthrough: E710 increments EDI (type index), advances ESI (snapshot cursor) by12, then loops or proceeds to CurrentPlayer checks.
callers.caller_stack_contract: Caller E690 has saved EBX,ESI,EDI on its real stack; all remain live across this call. It has not saved EBP locally. EDI is required for correct loop indexing.
callers.EIP_only_after_damage: After E530 has run, EDI=0 destroys the loop index; ESP no longer names the saved-register frame, and EBP=0 is not restored by E690's local epilogue.
callers.hypothetical_return_before_damage: If control returns before E530 changes any state, a normal return balances the single CALL-pushed return address. This caller supplied no additional stack arguments to this routine. The shown fallthrough exists and does not inspect E530's EAX result or condition flags.

callers.EIP_only_after_damage: ESP now points outside that real frame, so POP EBX and the saved-ECX load cannot restore the intended values. EBP and EDI were already restored before the call, then destroyed by E530, with no later restoration in this caller.

conclusions.before_damage: The four callsites retain normal continuation code, and no additional E530 stack-argument cleanup is required. A purely hypothetical return before any destructive instructions preserves the caller frame; this local ABI observation is not proof of a supported or safe game continuation.
conclusions.after_damage_EIP_only: E530 has replaced ESP, zeroed EDI and EBP, and changed ECX/EAX before its final invalid jump. Advancing only EIP to a caller continuation leaves wrong stack and nonvolatile register state; the documented loops, CALLs, POPs and return paths do not repair it.
conclusions.not_repaired_by_return: An early return would not restore altered game code/data, refresh integrity baselines, repair network/event identity checks, roll back simulation state, or establish multiplayer synchronization. Subsequent independent checks remain present.
conclusions.noreturn_claim: No evidence here supports claiming the compiler removed all post-call continuations due to noreturn optimization.
conclusions.not_established: User's loaded binary, live fault/exception context, whether any of these four branches fired, or whether returning from one would recover the observed user failure.
